/**
 * OpenCode in-sandbox runner.
 *
 * This file is shipped INTO the sandbox by the orchestrator and executed there as
 * `node __agent_eval__/run.mjs '<AgentRunInput JSON>'`. It is intentionally
 * ZERO-DEPENDENCY (only `node:*` builtins) because the sandbox only has the
 * fixture's own deps + the installed `opencode` CLI — it cannot import anything
 * from the @vercel/agent-eval package.
 *
 * Dual mode:
 *   - runnable: invoked directly → reads argv, runs the agent, writes the result
 *     file + prints a status line, exits 0.
 *   - importable: `import { runAgent } from './run.mjs'` → returns a RunnerResult
 *     (no file write, no exit). This is what a future in-sandbox judge reuses.
 *
 * The pure helpers below are exported (not just `runAgent`) so they can be
 * unit-tested directly — the same code the sandbox runs (see opencode.test.ts).
 */

import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';

Welcome to the Next.js documentation!

## What is Next.js?

Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. You use React Components to build user interfaces, and Next.js for additional features and optimizations.

It also automatically configures lower-level tools like bundlers and compilers. You can instead focus on building your product and shipping quickly.

Whether you're an individual developer or part of a larger team, Next.js can help you build interactive, dynamic, and fast React applications.

## How to use the docs

The docs are organized into 3 sections:

- [Getting Started](/docs/app/getting-started): Step-by-step tutorials to help you create a new application and learn the core Next.js features.
- [Guides](/docs/app/guides): Tutorials on specific use cases, choose what's relevant to you.
- [API Reference](/docs/app/api-reference): Detailed technical reference for every feature.

Use the sidebar to navigate through the sections, or search (`Ctrl+K` or `Cmd+K`) to quickly find a page.

## App Router and Pages Router

Next.js has two different routers:

- **App Router**: The newer router that supports new React features like Server Components.
- **Pages Router**: The original router, still supported and being improved.

At the top of the sidebar, you'll notice a dropdown menu that allows you to switch between the [App Router](/docs/app) and the [Pages Router](/docs/pages) docs.

### React version handling

The App Router and Pages Router handle React versions differently:

- **App Router**: Uses [React canary releases](https://react.dev/blog/2023/05/03/react-canaries) built-in, which include all the stable React 19 changes, as well as newer features being validated in frameworks, prior to a new React release.

- **Pages Router**: Uses the React version installed in your project's `package.json`.

This approach ensures new React features work reliably in the App Router while maintaining backwards compatibility for existing Pages Router applications.

## Pre-requisite knowledge

Our documentation assumes some familiarity with web development. Before getting started, it'll help if you're comfortable with:

- HTML
- CSS
- JavaScript
- React

If you're new to React or need a refresher, we recommend starting with our [React Foundations course](/learn/react-foundations), and the [Next.js Foundations course](/learn/dashboard-app) that has you building an application as you learn.

## Accessibility

For the best experience when using a screen reader, we recommend using Firefox and NVDA, or Safari and VoiceOver.

## Join our Community

If you have questions about anything related to Next.js, you're always welcome to ask our community on [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions), [Discord](https://discord.com/invite/bUG2bvbtHy), [X (Twitter)](https://x.com/nextjs), and [Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/nextjs).

00002| title: generateStaticParams
00003| description: API reference for the generateStaticParams function.
00004| ---
00005| 
00006| The `generateStaticParams` function can be used in combination with [dynamic route segments](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) to [**statically generate**](/docs/app/glossary#prerendering) routes at build time instead of on-demand at request time.
00007| 
00008| `generateStaticParams` can be used with:
00009| 
00010| - [Pages](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) (`page.tsx`/`page.js`)
00011| - [Layouts](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout) (`layout.tsx`/`layout.js`)
00012| - [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) (`route.ts`/`route.js`)
00013| 
00014| ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
00015| // Return a list of `params` to populate the [slug] dynamic segment
00016| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00017|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00018| 
00019|   return posts.map((post) => ({
00020|     slug: post.slug,
00021|   }))
00022| }
00023| 
00024| // Multiple versions of this page will be statically generated
00025| // using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
00026| export default async function Page({
00027|   params,
00028| }: {
00029|   params: Promise<{ slug: string }>
00030| }) {
00031|   const { slug } = await params
00032|   // ...
00033| }
00034| ```
00035| 
00036| ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
00037| // Return a list of `params` to populate the [slug] dynamic segment
00038| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00039|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00040| 
00041|   return posts.map((post) => ({
00042|     slug: post.slug,
00043|   }))
00044| }
00045| 
00046| // Multiple versions of this page will be statically generated
00047| // using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
00048| export default async function Page({ params }) {
00049|   const { slug } = await params
00050|   // ...
00051| }
00052| ```
00053| 
00054| > **Good to know**:
00055| >
00056| > - You can use the [`dynamicParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/dynamicParams) segment config option to control what happens when a dynamic segment is visited that was not generated with `generateStaticParams`.
00057| > - A dynamic route that uses [`ensureStatic = 'navigation'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/ensureStatic#navigation) must return at least one params object, and every object must include all dynamic parameters for the route. See the [`generateStaticParams` error guide](/docs/messages/generate-static-params#with-ensurestatic).
00058| > - You must return [an empty array from `generateStaticParams`](#all-paths-at-runtime) or utilize [`export const dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic) in order to revalidate (ISR) [paths at runtime](#all-paths-at-runtime).
00059| > - During `next dev`, `generateStaticParams` will be called when you navigate to a route.
00060| > - During `next build`, `generateStaticParams` runs before the corresponding Layouts or Pages are generated.
00061| > - During revalidation (ISR), `generateStaticParams` will not be called again.
00062| > - `generateStaticParams` replaces the [`getStaticPaths`](/docs/pages/api-reference/functions/get-static-paths) function in the Pages Router.
00063| 
00064| ## Parameters
00065| 
00066| `options.params` (optional)
00067| 
00068| If multiple dynamic segments in a route use `generateStaticParams`, the child `generateStaticParams` function is executed once for each set of `params` the parent generates.
00069| 
00070| The `params` object contains the populated `params` from the parent `generateStaticParams`, which can be used to [generate the `params` in a child segment](#multiple-dynamic-segments-in-a-route).
00071| 
00072| ## Returns
00073| 
00074| `generateStaticParams` should return an array of objects where each object represents the populated dynamic segments of a single route.
00075| 
00076| - Each property in the object is a dynamic segment to be filled in for the route.
00077| - The properties name is the segment's name, and the properties value is what that segment should be filled in with.
00078| 
00079| | Example Route                    | `generateStaticParams` Return Type        |
00080| | -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
00081| | `/product/[id]`                  | `{ id: string }[]`                        |
00082| | `/products/[category]/[product]` | `{ category: string, product: string }[]` |
00083| | `/products/[...slug]`            | `{ slug: string[] }[]`                    |
00084| 
00085| ## Single Dynamic Segment
00086| 
00087| ```tsx filename="app/product/[id]/page.tsx" switcher
00088| export function generateStaticParams() {
00089|   return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
00090| }
00091| 
00092| // Three versions of this page will be statically generated
00093| // using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
00094| // - /product/1
00095| // - /product/2
00096| // - /product/3
00097| export default async function Page({
00098|   params,
00099| }: {
00100|   params: Promise<{ id: string }>
00101| }) {
00102|   const { id } = await params
00103|   // ...
00104| }
00105| ```
00106| 
00107| ```jsx filename="app/product/[id]/page.js" switcher
00108| export function generateStaticParams() {
00109|   return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
00110| }
00111| 
00112| // Three versions of this page will be statically generated
00113| // using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
00114| // - /product/1
00115| // - /product/2
00116| // - /product/3
00117| export default async function Page({ params }) {
00118|   const { id } = await params
00119|   // ...
00120| }
00121| ```
00122| 
00123| ## Multiple Dynamic Segments
00124| 
00125| ```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
00126| export function generateStaticParams() {
00127|   return [
00128|     { category: 'a', product: '1' },
00129|     { category: 'b', product: '2' },
00130|     { category: 'c', product: '3' },
00131|   ]
00132| }
00133| 
00134| // Three versions of this page will be statically generated
00135| // using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
00136| // - /products/a/1
00137| // - /products/b/2
00138| // - /products/c/3
00139| export default async function Page({
00140|   params,
00141| }: {
00142|   params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
00143| }) {
00144|   const { category, product } = await params
00145|   // ...
00146| }
00147| ```
00148| 
00149| ```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js" switcher
00150| export function generateStaticParams() {
00151|   return [
00152|     { category: 'a', product: '1' },
00153|     { category: 'b', product: '2' },
00154|     { category: 'c', product: '3' },
00155|   ]
00156| }
00157| 
00158| // Three versions of this page will be statically generated
00159| // using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
00160| // - /products/a/1
00161| // - /products/b/2
00162| // - /products/c/3
00163| export default async function Page({ params }) {
00164|   const { category, product } = await params
00165|   // ...
00166| }
00167| ```
00168| 
00169| ## Catch-all Dynamic Segment
00170| 
00171| ```tsx filename="app/product/[...slug]/page.tsx" switcher
00172| export function generateStaticParams() {
00173|   return [{ slug: ['a', '1'] }, { slug: ['b', '2'] }, { slug: ['c', '3'] }]
00174| }
00175| 
00176| // Three versions of this page will be statically generated
00177| // using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
00178| // - /product/a/1
00179| // - /product/b/2
00180| // - /product/c/3
00181| export default async function Page({
00182|   params,
00183| }: {
00184|   params: Promise<{ slug: string[] }>
00185| }) {
00186|   const { slug } = await params
00187|   // ...
00188| }
00189| ```
00190| 
00191| ```jsx filename="app/product/[...slug]/page.js" switcher
00192| export function generateStaticParams() {
00193|   return [{ slug: ['a', '1'] }, { slug: ['b', '2'] }, { slug: ['c', '3'] }]
00194| }
00195| 
00196| // Three versions of this page will be statically generated
00197| // using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
00198| // - /product/a/1
00199| // - /product/b/2
00200| // - /product/c/3
00201| export default async function Page({ params }) {
00202|   const { slug } = await params
00203|   // ...
00204| }
00205| ```
00206| 
00207| ## Examples
00208| 
00209| ### Prerendering
00210| 
00211| #### All paths at build time
00212| 
00213| To statically render all paths at build time, supply the full list of paths to `generateStaticParams`:
00214| 
00215| ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
00216| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00217|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00218| 
00219|   return posts.map((post) => ({
00220|     slug: post.slug,
00221|   }))
00222| }
00223| ```
00224| 
00225| ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
00226| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00227|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00228| 
00229|   return posts.map((post) => ({
00230|     slug: post.slug,
00231|   }))
00232| }
00233| ```
00234| 
00235| #### Subset of paths at build time
00236| 
00237| To statically render a subset of paths at build time, and the rest the first time they're visited at runtime, return a partial list of paths:
00238| 
00239| ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
00240| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00241|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00242| 
00243|   // Render the first 10 posts at build time
00244|   return posts.slice(0, 10).map((post) => ({
00245|     slug: post.slug,
00246|   }))
00247| }
00248| ```
00249| 
00250| ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
00251| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00252|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00253| 
00254|   // Render the first 10 posts at build time
00255|   return posts.slice(0, 10).map((post) => ({
00256|     slug: post.slug,
00257|   }))
00258| }
00259| ```
00260| 
00261| Then, by using the [`dynamicParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/dynamicParams) segment config option, you can control what happens when a dynamic segment is visited that was not generated with `generateStaticParams`.
00262| 
00263| ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
00264| // All posts besides the top 10 will be a 404
00265| export const dynamicParams = false
00266| 
00267| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00268|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00269|   const topPosts = posts.slice(0, 10)
00270| 
00271|   return topPosts.map((post) => ({
00272|     slug: post.slug,
00273|   }))
00274| }
00275| ```
00276| 
00277| ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
00278| // All posts besides the top 10 will be a 404
00279| export const dynamicParams = false
00280| 
00281| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00282|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00283|   const topPosts = posts.slice(0, 10)
00284| 
00285|   return topPosts.map((post) => ({
00286|     slug: post.slug,
00287|   }))
00288| }
00289| ```
00290| 
00291| #### All paths at runtime
00292| 
00293| To statically render all paths the first time they're visited, return an empty array (no paths will be rendered at build time) or utilize [`export const dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic):
00294| 
00295| ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js"
00296| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00297|   return []
00298| }
00299| ```
00300| 
00301| > **Good to know:**
00302| >
00303| > - You must always return an array from `generateStaticParams`, even if it's empty. Otherwise, the route will be dynamically rendered.
00304| 
00305| ```jsx filename="app/changelog/[slug]/page.js"
00306| export const dynamic = 'force-static'
00307| ```
00308| 
00309| #### With Cache Components
00310| 
00311| When using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) with dynamic routes, `generateStaticParams` must return **at least one param**. Empty arrays cause a [build error](/docs/messages/empty-generate-static-params). This allows Cache Components to validate your route doesn't incorrectly access `cookies()`, `headers()`, or `searchParams` at runtime.
00312| 
00313| > **Good to know**: If you don't know the actual param values at build time, you can return a placeholder param (e.g., `[{ slug: '__placeholder__' }]`) for validation, then handle it in your page with `notFound()`. However, this prevents build time validation from working effectively and may cause runtime errors.
00314| 
00315| See the [dynamic routes section](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes#with-cache-components) for detailed walkthroughs, or [ISR with Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components) for prerendering a subset of routes and serving App Shells for the rest.
00316| 
00317| ### With Route Handlers
00318| 
00319| You can use `generateStaticParams` with [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) to statically generate API responses at build time:
00320| 
00321| ```ts filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts" switcher
00322| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00323|   return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
00324| }
00325| 
00326| export async function GET(
00327|   request: Request,
00328|   { params }: RouteContext<'/api/posts/[id]'>
00329| ) {
00330|   const { id } = await params
00331|   // This will be statically generated for IDs 1, 2, and 3
00332|   return Response.json({ id, title: `Post ${id}` })
00333| }
00334| ```
00335| 
00336| ```js filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.js" switcher
00337| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00338|   return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
00339| }
00340| 
00341| export async function GET(request, { params }) {
00342|   const { id } = await params
00343|   // This will be statically generated for IDs 1, 2, and 3
00344|   return Response.json({ id, title: `Post ${id}` })
00345| }
00346| ```
00347| 
00348| ### Route Handlers with Cache Components
00349| 
00350| When using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching), combine with `use cache` for optimal caching:
00351| 
00352| ```ts filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts"
00353| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00354|   return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
00355| }
00356| 
00357| async function getPost(id: Promise<string>) {
00358|   'use cache'
00359|   const resolvedId = await id
00360|   const response = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/posts/${resolvedId}`)
00361|   return response.json()
00362| }
00363| 
00364| export async function GET(
00365|   request: Request,
00366|   { params }: RouteContext<'/api/posts/[id]'>
00367| ) {
00368|   const post = await getPost(params.then((p) => p.id))
00369|   return Response.json(post)
00370| }
00371| ```
00372| 
00373| See the [Route Handlers documentation](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route#static-generation-with-generatestaticparams) for more details.
00374| 
00375| ### Disable rendering for unspecified paths
00376| 
00377| To prevent unspecified paths from being prerendered at runtime, add the `export const dynamicParams = false` option in a route segment. When this config option is used, only paths provided by `generateStaticParams` will be served, and unspecified routes will 404 or match (in the case of [catch-all routes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes#catch-all-segments)).
00378| 
00379| ### Multiple Dynamic Segments in a Route
00380| 
00381| You can generate params for dynamic segments above the current layout or page, but **not below**. For example, given the `app/products/[category]/[product]` route:
00382| 
00383| - `app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js` can generate params for **both** `[category]` and `[product]`.
00384| - `app/products/[category]/layout.js` can **only** generate params for `[category]`.
00385| 
00386| There are two approaches to generating params for a route with multiple dynamic segments:
00387| 
00388| #### Generate params from the bottom up
00389| 
00390| Generate multiple dynamic segments from the child route segment.
00391| 
00392| ```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
00393| // Generate segments for both [category] and [product]
00394| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00395|   const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
00396| 
00397|   return products.map((product) => ({
00398|     category: product.category.slug,
00399|     product: product.id,
00400|   }))
00401| }
00402| 
00403| export default function Page({
00404|   params,
00405| }: {
00406|   params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
00407| }) {
00408|   // ...
00409| }
00410| ```
00411| 
00412| ```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js" switcher
00413| // Generate segments for both [category] and [product]
00414| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00415|   const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
00416| 
00417|   return products.map((product) => ({
00418|     category: product.category.slug,
00419|     product: product.id,
00420|   }))
00421| }
00422| 
00423| export default function Page({ params }) {
00424|   // ...
00425| }
00426| ```
00427| 
00428| #### Generate params from the top down
00429| 
00430| Generate the parent segments first and use the result to generate the child segments.
00431| 
00432| ```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/layout.tsx" switcher
00433| // Generate segments for [category]
00434| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00435|   const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
00436| 
00437|   return products.map((product) => ({
00438|     category: product.category.slug,
00439|   }))
00440| }
00441| 
00442| export default function Layout({
00443|   params,
00444| }: {
00445|   params: Promise<{ category: string }>
00446| }) {
00447|   // ...
00448| }
00449| ```
00450| 
00451| ```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/layout.js" switcher
00452| // Generate segments for [category]
00453| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00454|   const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
00455| 
00456|   return products.map((product) => ({
00457|     category: product.category.slug,
00458|   }))
00459| }
00460| 
00461| export default function Layout({ params }) {
00462|   // ...
00463| }
00464| ```
00465| 
00466| A child route segment's `generateStaticParams` function is executed once for each segment a parent `generateStaticParams` generates.
00467| 
00468| The child `generateStaticParams` function can use the `params` returned from the parent `generateStaticParams` function to dynamically generate its own segments.
00469| 
00470| ```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
00471| // Generate segments for [product] using the `params` passed from
00472| // the parent segment's `generateStaticParams` function
00473| export async function generateStaticParams({
00474|   params: { category },
00475| }: {
00476|   params: { category: string }
00477| }) {
00478|   const products = await fetch(
00479|     `https://.../products?category=${category}`
00480|   ).then((res) => res.json())
00481| 
00482|   return products.map((product) => ({
00483|     product: product.id,
00484|   }))

00042| ## `generateMetadata` function
00043| 
00044| Dynamic metadata depends on **dynamic information**, such as the current route parameters, external data, or `metadata` in parent segments, can be set by exporting a `generateMetadata` function that returns a [`Metadata` object](#metadata-fields).
00045| 
00046| Resolving `generateMetadata` is part of rendering the page. If the page can be prerendered and `generateMetadata` doesn't introduce dynamic behavior, the resulting metadata is included in the page's initial HTML.

00048| Otherwise the metadata resolved from `generateMetadata` [can be streamed](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#streaming-metadata) after sending the initial UI.

00050| ```tsx filename="app/products/[id]/page.tsx" switcher

00052| 
00053| type Props = {
00054|   params: Promise<{ id: string }>
00055|   searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }>

00057|

00059|   { params, searchParams }: Props,
00060|   parent: ResolvingMetadata

00063|   const { id } = await params
00064| 
00065|   // fetch data
00066|   const product = await fetch(`https://.../${id}`).then((res) => res.json())
00067|

00069|   const previousImages = (await parent).openGraph?.images || []

00072|     title: product.title,
00073|     openGraph: {
00074|       images: ['/some-specific-page-image.jpg', ...previousImages],

00081|

00165| ### Parameters

00171|

00195| > - `fetch` requests are automatically memoized for the same data across `generateMetadata`, `generateStaticParams`, Layouts, Pages, and Server Components. React [`cache` can be used](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) if `fetch` is unavailable.
00196| > - `searchParams` are only available in `page.js` segments.
00197| > - The [`redirect()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/redirect) and [`notFound()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) Next.js methods can also be used inside `generateMetadata`.
00198| 
00199| ### Metadata Fields
00200| 
00201| The following fields are supported:
00202| 
00203| #### `title`
00204| 
00205| The `title` attribute is used to set the title of the document. It can be defined as a simple [string](#string) or an optional [template object](#template).
00206| 
00207| ##### String
00208| 
00209| ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js"
00210| export const metadata = {
00211|   title: 'Next.js',
00212| }
00213| ```
00214| 
00215| ```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
00216| <title>Next.js</title>
00217| ```
00218| 
00219| ##### `default`
00220| 
00221| `title.default` can be used to provide a **fallback title** to child route segments that don't define a `title`.
00222| 
00223| ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx"
00224| import type { Metadata } from 'next'
00225| 
00226| export const metadata: Metadata = {
00227|   title: {
00228|     default: 'Acme',
00229|   },
00230| }
00231| ```
00232| 
00233| ```tsx filename="app/about/page.tsx"
00234| import type { Metadata } from 'next'
00235| 
00236| export const metadata: Metadata = {}
00237| 
00238| // Output: <title>Acme</title>
00239| ```
00240| 
00241| ##### `template`
00242| 
00243| `title.template` can be used to add a prefix or a suffix to `titles` defined in **child** route segments.
00244| 
00245| ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher
00246| import type { Metadata } from 'next'
00247| 
00248| export const metadata: Metadata = {
00249|   title: {
00250|     template: '%s | Acme',
00251|     default: 'Acme', // a default is required when creating a template
00252|   },
00253| }
00254| ```
00255| 
00256| ```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher
00257| export const metadata = {
00258|   title: {
00259|     template: '%s | Acme',
00260|     default: 'Acme', // a default is required when creating a template
00261|   },
00262| }
00263| ```
00264| 
00265| ```tsx filename="app/about/page.tsx" switcher
00266| import type { Metadata } from 'next'
00267| 
00268| export const metadata: Metadata = {
00269|   title: 'About',
00270| }
00271| 
00272| // Output: <title>About | Acme</title>
00273| ```
00274| 
00275| ```jsx filename="app/about/page.js" switcher
00276| export const metadata = {
00277|   title: 'About',
00278| }
00279| 
00280| // Output: <title>About | Acme</title>
00281| ```
00282| 
00283| > **Good to know**:
00284| >
00285| > - `title.template` applies to **child** route segments and **not** the segment it's defined in. This means:
00286| >   - `title.default` is **required** when you add a `title.template`.
00287| >   - `title.template` defined in `layout.js` will not apply to a `title` defined in a `page.js` of the same route segment.
00288| >   - `title.template` defined in `page.js` has no effect because a page is always the terminating segment (it doesn't have any children route segments).
00289| > - `title.template` has **no effect** if a route has not defined a `title` or `title.default`.
00290| 
00291| ##### `absolute`
00292| 
00293| `title.absolute` can be used to provide a title that **ignores** `title.template` set in parent segments.
00294| 
00295| ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher
00296| import type { Metadata } from 'next'
00297| 
00298| export const metadata: Metadata = {
00299|   title: {
00300|     template: '%s | Acme',
00301|   },
00302| }
00303| ```
00304| 
00305| ```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher
00306| export const metadata = {
00307|   title: {
00308|     template: '%s | Acme',
00309|   },
00310| }
00311| ```
00312| 
00313| ```tsx filename="app/about/page.tsx" switcher
00314| import type { Metadata } from 'next'
00315| 
00316| export const metadata: Metadata = {
00317|   title: {
00318|     absolute: 'About',
00319|   },
00320| }
00321| 
00322| // Output: <title>About</title>
00323| ```
00324| 
00325| ```jsx filename="app/about/page.js" switcher
00326| export const metadata = {
00327|   title: {
00328|     absolute: 'About',
00329|   },
00330| }
00331| 
00332| // Output: <title>About</title>
00333| ```
00334| 
00335| > **Good to know**:
00336| >
00337| > - `layout.js`
00338| >   - `title` (string) and `title.default` define the default title for child segments (that do not define their own `title`). It will augment `title.template` from the closest parent segment if it exists.
00339| >   - `title.absolute` defines the default title for child segments. It ignores `title.template` from parent segments.
00340| >   - `title.template` defines a new title template for child segments.
00341| > - `page.js`
00342| >   - If a page does not define its own title the closest parents resolved title will be used.
00343| >   - `title` (string) defines the routes title. It will augment `title.template` from the closest parent segment if it exists.
00344| >   - `title.absolute` defines the route title. It ignores `title.template` from parent segments.
00345| >   - `title.template` has no effect in `page.js` because a page is always the terminating segment of a route.
00346| 
00347| ### `description`
00348| 
00349| ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js"
00350| export const metadata = {
00351|   description: 'The React Framework for the Web',
00352| }
00353| ```

00355| ```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
00356| <meta name="description" content="The React Framework for the Web" />
00357| ```
00358| 
00359| ### Other fields
00360| 
00361| ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js"
00362| export const metadata = {
00363|   generator: 'Next.js',
00364|   applicationName: 'Next.js',
00365|   referrer: 'origin-when-cross-origin',
00366|   keywords: ['Next.js', 'React', 'JavaScript'],
00367|   authors: [{ name: 'Seb' }, { name: 'Josh', url: 'https://nextjs.org' }],
00368|   creator: 'Jiachi Liu',
00369|   publisher: 'Sebastian Markbåge',
00370|   formatDetection: {
00371|     email: false,
00372|     address: false,
00373|     telephone: false,
00374|   },
00375| }
00376| ```
00377| 
00378| ```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
00379| <meta name="application-name" content="Next.js" />
00380| <meta name="author" content="Seb" />
00381| <link rel="author" href="https://nextjs.org" />
00382| <meta name="author" content="Josh" />
00383| <meta name="generator" content="Next.js" />
00384| <meta name="keywords" content="Next.js,React,JavaScript" />
00385| <meta name="referrer" content="origin-when-cross-origin" />
00386| <meta name="creator" content="Jiachi Liu" />
00387| <meta name="publisher" content="Sebastian Markbåge" />
00388| <meta name="format-detection" content="telephone=no, address=no, email=no" />
00389| ```
00390| 
00391| #### `metadataBase`
00392| 
00393| `metadataBase` is a convenience option to set a base URL prefix for `metadata` fields that require a fully qualified URL.
00394| 
00395| - `metadataBase` allows URL-based `metadata` fields defined in the **current route segment and below** to use a **relative path** instead of an otherwise required absolute URL.
00396| - The field's relative path will be composed with `metadataBase` to form a fully qualified URL.
00397| 
00398| ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js"
00399| export const metadata = {
00400|   metadataBase: new URL('https://acme.com'),
00401|   alternates: {
00402|     canonical: '/',
00403|     languages: {
00404|       'en-US': '/en-US',
00405|       'de-DE': '/de-DE',
00406|     },
00407|   },
00408|   openGraph: {
00409|     images: '/og-image.png',
00410|   },
00411| }
00412| ```
00413| 
00414| ```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
00415| <link rel="canonical" href="https://acme.com" />
00416| <link rel="alternate" hreflang="en-US" href="https://acme.com/en-US" />
00417| <link rel="alternate" hreflang="de-DE" href="https://acme.com/de-DE" />
00418| <meta property="og:image" content="https://acme.com/og-image.png" />
00419| ```
00420| 
00421| > **Good to know**:
00422| >
00423| > - `metadataBase` is typically set in root `app/layout.js` to apply to URL-based `metadata` fields across all routes.
00424| > - When `generateMetadata` uses `'use cache'`, its return value must be serializable. `URL` instances are not supported by Cache Functions, so values such as `metadataBase` should be returned as strings (for example, `url.toString()`). See [`use cache` serialization requirements](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#serialization).
00425| > - All URL-based `metadata` fields that require absolute URLs can be configured with a `metadataBase` option.
00426| > - `metadataBase` can contain a subdomain e.g. `https://app.acme.com` or base path e.g. `https://acme.com/start/from/here`
00427| > - If a `metadata` field provides an absolute URL, `metadataBase` will be ignored.
00428| > - Using a relative path in a URL-based `metadata` field without configuring a `metadataBase` will cause a build error.
00429| > - Next.js will normalize duplicate slashes between `metadataBase` (e.g. `https://acme.com/`) and a relative field (e.g. `/path`) to a single slash (e.g. `https://acme.com/path`)
00430| 
00431| #### URL Composition
00432| 
00433| URL composition favors developer intent over default directory traversal semantics.
00434| 
00435| - Trailing slashes between `metadataBase` and `metadata` fields are normalized.
00436| - An "absolute" path in a `metadata` field (that typically would replace the whole URL path) is treated as a "relative" path (starting from the end of `metadataBase`).
00437| 
00438| For example, given the following `metadataBase`:
00439| 
00440| ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher
00441| import type { Metadata } from 'next'
00442| 
00443| export const metadata: Metadata = {
00444|   metadataBase: new URL('https://acme.com'),
00445| }
00446| ```
00447| 
00448| ```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher
00449| export const metadata = {
00450|   metadataBase: new URL('https://acme.com'),
00451| }
00452| ```
00453| 
00454| Any `metadata` fields that inherit the above `metadataBase` and set their own value will be resolved as follows:
00455| 
00456| | `metadata` field                 | Resolved URL                     |
00457| | -------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
00458| | `/`                              | `https://acme.com`               |
00459| | `./`                             | `https://acme.com`               |
00460| | `payments`                       | `https://acme.com/payments`      |
00461| | `/payments`                      | `https://acme.com/payments`      |
00462| | `./payments`                     | `https://acme.com/payments`      |
00463| | `../payments`                    | `https://acme.com/payments`      |
00464| | `https://beta.acme.com/payments` | `https://beta.acme.com/payments` |
00465| 
00466| ### `openGraph`
00467| 
00468| ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js"
00469| export const metadata = {
00470|   openGraph: {
00471|     title: 'Next.js',
00472|     description: 'The React Framework for the Web',
00473|     url: 'https://nextjs.org',
00474|     siteName: 'Next.js',
00475|     images: [
00476|       {

01048| ### Types
01049| 
01050| You can add type safety to your metadata by using the `Metadata` type. If you are using the [built-in TypeScript plugin](/docs/app/api-reference/config/typescript) in your IDE, you do not need to manually add the type, but you can still explicitly add it if you want.
01051| 
01052| #### `metadata` object
01053| 
01054| ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx"
01055| import type { Metadata } from 'next'
01056| 
01057| export const metadata: Metadata = {
01058|   title: 'Next.js',
01059| }
01060| ```
01061| 
01062| #### `generateMetadata` function
01063| 
01064| ##### Regular function
01065| 
01066| ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx"
01067| import type { Metadata } from 'next'
01068| 
01069| export function generateMetadata(): Metadata {
01070|   return {
01071|     title: 'Next.js',
01072|   }
01073| }
01074| ```
01075| 
01076| ##### Async function
01077| 
01078| ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx"
01079| import type { Metadata } from 'next'
01080| 
01081| export async function generateMetadata(): Promise<Metadata> {
01082|   return {
01083|     title: 'Next.js',
01084|   }
01085| }
01086| ```
01087| 
01088| ##### With segment props
01089| 
01090| ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx"
01091| import type { Metadata } from 'next'
01092| 
01093| type Props = {
01094|   params: Promise<{ id: string }>
01095|   searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }>
01096| }
01097| 
01098| export function generateMetadata({ params, searchParams }: Props): Metadata {
01099|   return {
01100|     title: 'Next.js',
01101|   }
01102| }
01103| 
01104| export default function Page({ params, searchParams }: Props) {}
01105| ```
01106| 
01107| ##### With parent metadata
01108| 
01109| ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx"
01110| import type { Metadata, ResolvingMetadata } from 'next'
01111| 
01112| export async function generateMetadata(
01113|   { params, searchParams }: Props,
01114|   parent: ResolvingMetadata
01115| ): Promise<Metadata> {
01116|   return {
01117|     title: 'Next.js',
01118|   }
01119| }
01120| ```
01121| 
01122| ##### JavaScript Projects
01123| 
01124| For JavaScript projects, you can use JSDoc to add type safety.
01125| 
01126| ```js filename="layout.js | page.js"
01127| /** @type {import("next").Metadata} */
01128| export const metadata = {
01129|   title: 'Next.js',
01130| }
01131| ```
01132| 
01133| ### Unsupported Metadata
01134| 
01135| The following metadata types do not currently have built-in support. However, they can still be rendered in the layout or page itself.
01136| 
01137| | Metadata                      | Recommendation                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
01138| | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
01139| | `<meta http-equiv="...">`     | Use appropriate HTTP Headers via [`redirect()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/redirect), [Proxy](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy#nextresponse), [Security Headers](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/headers) |
01140| | `<base>`                      | Render the tag in the layout or page itself.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
01141| | `<noscript>`                  | Render the tag in the layout or page itself.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
01142| | `<style>`                     | Learn more about [styling in Next.js](/docs/app/getting-started/css).                                                                                                                                                                        |
01143| | `<script>`                    | Learn more about [using scripts](/docs/app/guides/scripts).                                                                                                                                                                                  |
01144| | `<link rel="stylesheet" />`   | `import` stylesheets directly in the layout or page itself.                                                                                                                                                                                  |
01145| | `<link rel="preload" />`      | Use [ReactDOM preload method](#link-relpreload)                                                                                                                                                                                              |
01146| | `<link rel="preconnect" />`   | Use [ReactDOM preconnect method](#link-relpreconnect)                                                                                                                                                                                        |
01147| | `<link rel="dns-prefetch" />` | Use [ReactDOM prefetchDNS method](#link-reldns-prefetch)                                                                                                                                                                                     |
01148| 
01149| ### Resource hints
01150| 
01151| The `<link>` element has a number of `rel` keywords that can be used to hint to the browser that an external resource is likely to be needed. The browser uses this information to apply preloading optimizations depending on the keyword.
01152| 
01153| While the Metadata API doesn't directly support these hints, you can use new [`ReactDOM` methods](https://github.com/facebook/react/pull/26237) to safely insert them into the `<head>` of the document.
01154| 
01155| ```tsx filename="app/preload-resources.tsx" switcher
01156| 'use client'
01157| 
01158| import ReactDOM from 'react-dom'
01159| 
01160| export function PreloadResources() {
01161|   ReactDOM.preload('...', { as: '...' })
01162|   ReactDOM.preconnect('...', { crossOrigin: '...' })
01163|   ReactDOM.prefetchDNS('...')
01164| 
01165|   return '...'
01166| }
01167| ```
01168| 
01169| ```jsx filename="app/preload-resources.js" switcher
01170| 'use client'
01171| 
01172| import ReactDOM from 'react-dom'
01173| 
01174| export function PreloadResources() {
01175|   ReactDOM.preload('...', { as: '...' })
01176|   ReactDOM.preconnect('...', { crossOrigin: '...' })
01177|   ReactDOM.prefetchDNS('...')
01178| 
01179|   return '...'
01180| }
01181| ```
01182| 
01183| #### `<link rel="preload">`
01184| 
01185| Start loading a resource early in the page rendering (browser) lifecycle. [MDN Docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/rel/preload).
01186| 
01187| ```tsx
01188| ReactDOM.preload(href: string, options: { as: string })
01189| ```
01190| 
01191| ```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
01192| <link rel="preload" href="..." as="..." />
01193| ```
01194| 
01195| ##### `<link rel="preconnect">`
01196| 
01197| Preemptively initiate a connection to an origin. [MDN Docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/rel/preconnect).
01198| 
01199| ```tsx
01200| ReactDOM.preconnect(href: string, options?: { crossOrigin?: string })
01201| ```
01202| 
01203| ```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
01204| <link rel="preconnect" href="..." crossorigin />
01205| ```
01206| 
01207| #### `<link rel="dns-prefetch">`
01208| 
01209| Attempt to resolve a domain name before resources get requested. [MDN Docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/rel/dns-prefetch).
01210| 
01211| ```tsx
01212| ReactDOM.prefetchDNS(href: string)
01213| ```
01214| 
01215| ```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
01216| <link rel="dns-prefetch" href="..." />
01217| ```
01218| 
01219| > **Good to know**:
01220| >
01221| > - These methods are currently only supported in Client Components, which are still Server Side Rendered on initial page load.
01222| > - Next.js in-built features such as `next/font`, `next/image` and `next/script` automatically handle relevant resource hints.
01223| 
01224| ## Behavior
01225| 
01226| ### Default Fields
01227| 
01228| There are two default `meta` tags that are always added even if a route doesn't define metadata:
01229| 
01230| - The [meta charset tag](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Element/meta#attr-charset) sets the character encoding for the website.
01231| - The [meta viewport tag](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Viewport_meta_tag) sets the viewport width and scale for the website to adjust for different devices.
01232| 
01233| ```html
01234| <meta charset="utf-8" />
01235| <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
01236| ```
01237| 
01238| > **Good to know**: You can overwrite the default [`viewport`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#viewport) meta tag.
01239| 
01240| ### Streaming metadata
01241| 
01242| Streaming metadata allows Next.js to render and send the initial UI to the browser, without waiting for `generateMetadata` to complete.
01243| 
01244| When `generateMetadata` resolves, the resulting metadata tags are appended to the `<body>` tag. We have verified that metadata is interpreted correctly by bots that execute JavaScript and inspect the full DOM (e.g. `Googlebot`).
01245| 
01246| For **HTML-limited bots** that can’t execute JavaScript (e.g. `facebookexternalhit`), metadata continues to block page rendering. The resulting metadata will be available in the `<head>` tag.
01247| 
01248| Next.js automatically detects **HTML-limited bots** by looking at the User Agent header. You can use the [`htmlLimitedBots`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/htmlLimitedBots) option in your Next.js config file to override the default [User Agent list](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/packages/next/src/shared/lib/router/utils/html-bots.ts).
01249| 
01250| To fully disable streaming metadata:
01251| 
01252| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
01253| import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
01254| 
01255| const config: NextConfig = {
01256|   htmlLimitedBots: /.*/,
01257| }
01258| 
01259| export default config
01260| ```
01261| 
01262| ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
01263| module.exports = {
01264|   htmlLimitedBots: /.*/,
01265| }
01266| ```
01267| 
01268| Streaming metadata improves perceived performance by reducing [TTFB](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Glossary/Time_to_first_byte) and can help lowering [LCP](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Glossary/Largest_contentful_paint) time.
01269| 
01270| Overriding `htmlLimitedBots` could lead to longer response times. Streaming metadata is an advanced feature, and the default should be sufficient for most cases.
01271| 
01272| ### With Cache Components
01273| 
01274| When [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) is enabled, `generateMetadata` follows the same rules as other components. If metadata accesses runtime data (`cookies()`, `headers()`, `params`, `searchParams`) or performs uncached data fetching, it defers to request time.
01275| 
01276| How Next.js handles this depends on the rest of your page:
01277| 
01278| - **If other parts also defer to request time**: Prerendering generates a static shell, and metadata streams in with other deferred content.
01279| - **If the page or layout is otherwise fully prerenderable**: Next.js requires an explicit choice: cache the data if possible, or signal that deferred rendering is intentional.
01280| 
01281| Streaming metadata at runtime while the rest of the page is fully prerenderable is not common. To ensure this behavior is intentional, an error is raised indicating which page or layout needs to be handled.
01282| 
01283| To resolve this, you have two options. If metadata depends on external data but not runtime data, use `use cache`:
01284| 
01285| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" highlight={2}
01286| export async function generateMetadata() {
01287|   'use cache'
01288|   const { title, description } = await db.query('site-metadata')
01289|   return { title, description }
01290| }
01291| ```
01292| 
01293| If metadata genuinely requires runtime data, add a dynamic marker component to your page:
01294| 
01295| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" highlight={11-14,19,31}
01296| import { Suspense } from 'react'
01297| import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
01298| import { connection } from 'next/server'
01299| 
01300| export async function generateMetadata() {
01301|   const token = (await cookies()).get('token')?.value
01302|   // ... use token to fetch personalized metadata
01303|   return { title: 'Personalized Title' }
01304| }
01305| 
01306| const Connection = async () => {
01307|   await connection()
01308|   return null
01309| }
01310| 
01311| async function DynamicMarker() {
01312|   return (
01313|     <Suspense>
01314|       <Connection />
01315|     </Suspense>
01316|   )
01317| }
01318| 
01319| export default function Page() {
01320|   // DO NOT place await connection() here
01321|   // doing so prevents the article tag content from
01322|   // being included in the static shell
01323|   return (
01324|     <>
01325|       <article>Static content</article>
01326|       <DynamicMarker />
01327|     </>
01328|   )
01329| }
01330| ```
01331| 
01332| The `DynamicMarker` component renders nothing but tells Next.js the page has intentional dynamic content. By wrapping it in Suspense, the static content still prerenders normally.
01333| 
01334| See [Next.js encountered runtime data in `generateMetadata()`](/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-metadata-runtime) and [Next.js encountered uncached data in `generateMetadata()`](/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-metadata-dynamic) for full fix options and trade-offs.
01335| 
01336| ### Ordering
01337| 
01338| Metadata is evaluated in order, starting from the root segment down to the segment closest to the final `page.js` segment. For example:
01339| 
01340| 1. `app/layout.tsx` (Root Layout)
01341| 2. `app/blog/layout.tsx` (Nested Blog Layout)
01342| 3. `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` (Blog Page)
01343| 
01344| ### Merging
01345| 
01346| Following the [evaluation order](#ordering), Metadata objects exported from multiple segments in the same route are **shallowly** merged together to form the final metadata output of a route. Duplicate keys are **replaced** based on their ordering.
01347| 
01348| This means metadata with nested fields such as [`openGraph`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#opengraph) and [`robots`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#robots) that are defined in an earlier segment are **overwritten** by the last segment to define them.
01349| 
01350| #### Overwriting fields
01351| 
01352| ```jsx filename="app/layout.js"
01353| export const metadata = {
01354|   title: 'Acme',
01355|   openGraph: {
01356|     title: 'Acme',
01357|     description: 'Acme is a...',
01358|   },
01359| }
01360| ```
01361| 
01362| ```jsx filename="app/blog/page.js"
01363| export const metadata = {
01364|   title: 'Blog',
01365|   openGraph: {
01366|     title: 'Blog',
01367|   },
01368| }
01369| 
01370| // Output:
01371| // <title>Blog</title>
01372| // <meta property="og:title" content="Blog" />
01373| ```
01374| 
01375| In the example above:
01376| 
01377| - `title` from `app/layout.js` is **replaced** by `title` in `app/blog/page.js`.
01378| - All `openGraph` fields from `app/layout.js` are **replaced** in `app/blog/page.js` because `app/blog/page.js` sets `openGraph` metadata. Note the absence of `openGraph.description`.
01379| 
01380| If you'd like to share some nested fields between segments while overwriting others, you can pull them out into a separate variable:
01381| 
01382| ```jsx filename="app/shared-metadata.js"
01383| export const openGraphImage = { images: ['http://...'] }
01384| ```
01385| 
01386| ```jsx filename="app/page.js"
01387| import { openGraphImage } from './shared-metadata'
01388| 
01389| export const metadata = {
01390|   openGraph: {
01391|     ...openGraphImage,
01392|     title: 'Home',
01393|   },
01394| }
01395| ```
01396| 
01397| ```jsx filename="app/about/page.js"
01398| import { openGraphImage } from '../shared-metadata'
01399| 
01400| export const metadata = {
01401|   openGraph: {
01402|     ...openGraphImage,
01403|     title: 'About',
01404|   },
01405| }
01406| ```
01407| 
01408| In the example above, the OG image is shared between `app/layout.js` and `app/about/page.js` while the titles are different.
01409| 
01410| #### Inheriting fields
01411| 
01412| ```jsx filename="app/layout.js"
01413| export const metadata = {
01414|   title: 'Acme',
01415|   openGraph: {
01416|     title: 'Acme',
01417|     description: 'Acme is a...',
01418|   },
01419| }
01420| ```
01421| 
01422| ```jsx filename="app/about/page.js"
01423| export const metadata = {
01424|   title: 'About',
01425| }
01426| 
01427| // Output:
01428| // <title>About</title>
01429| // <meta property="og:title" content="Acme" />
01430| // <meta property="og:description" content="Acme is a..." />
01431| ```
01432| 
01433| **Notes**
01434| 
01435| - `title` from `app/layout.js` is **replaced** by `title` in `app/about/page.js`.
01436| - All `openGraph` fields from `app/layout.js` are **inherited** in `app/about/page.js` because `app/about/page.js` doesn't set `openGraph` metadata.
01437| 
01438| ## Version History
01439| 
01440| | Version   | Changes                                                                                                                                                 |
01441| | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
01442| | `v15.2.0` | Introduced streaming support to `generateMetadata`.                                                                                                     |
01443| | `v14.0.0` | `viewport`, `themeColor`, and `colorScheme` deprecated in favor of the [`viewport` configuration](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-viewport). |
01444| | `v13.2.0` | `metadata` and `generateMetadata` introduced.                                                                                                           |
01445|

00008| NextResponse extends the [Web Response API](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Response) with additional convenience methods.

00010| ## `cookies`
00011| 
00012| Read or mutate the [`Set-Cookie`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Set-Cookie) header of the response.
00013| 
00014| ### `set(name, value)`
00015| 
00016| Given a name, set a cookie with the given value on the response.
00017| 
00018| ```ts
00019| // Given incoming request /home
00020| let response = NextResponse.next()
00021| // Set a cookie to hide the banner
00022| response.cookies.set('show-banner', 'false')
00023| // Response will have a `Set-Cookie:show-banner=false;path=/home` header

00027| ### `get(name)`
00028| 
00029| Given a cookie name, return the value of the cookie. If the cookie is not found, `undefined` is returned. If multiple cookies are found, the first one is returned.

00033| let response = NextResponse.next()
00034| // { name: 'show-banner', value: 'false', Path: '/home' }
00035| response.cookies.get('show-banner')
00036| ```
00037| 
00038| ### `getAll()`
00039| 
00040| Given a cookie name, return the values of the cookie. If no name is given, return all cookies on the response.
00041|

00043| // Given incoming request /home
00044| let response = NextResponse.next()
00045| // [
00046| //   { name: 'experiments', value: 'new-pricing-page', Path: '/home' },
00047| //   { name: 'experiments', value: 'winter-launch', Path: '/home' },
00048| // ]
00049| response.cookies.getAll('experiments')
00050| // Alternatively, get all cookies for the response
00051| response.cookies.getAll()
00052| ```
00053| 
00054| ### `has(name)`
00055| 
00056| Given a cookie name, return `true` if the cookie exists on the response.
00057| 
00058| ```ts
00059| // Given incoming request /home
00060| let response = NextResponse.next()
00061| // Returns true if cookie exists, false if it does not
00062| response.cookies.has('experiments')
00063| ```
00064| 
00065| ### `delete(name)`
00066| 
00067| Given a cookie name, delete the cookie from the response.
00068|

00072| // Returns true for deleted, false if nothing is deleted
00073| response.cookies.delete('experiments')

00076| ## `json()`
00077| 
00078| Produce a response with the given JSON body.
00079| 
00080| ```ts filename="app/api/route.ts" switcher
00081| import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
00082| 
00083| export async function GET(request: Request) {

00089| import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'

00093| }

00096| ## `redirect()`
00097| 
00098| Produce a response that redirects to a [URL](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/URL).

00101| import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
00102| 
00103| return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/new', request.url))
00104| ```

00108| ```ts
00109| import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
00110| 
00111| // Given an incoming request...
00112| const loginUrl = new URL('/login', request.url)
00113| // Add ?from=/incoming-url to the /login URL
00114| loginUrl.searchParams.set('from', request.nextUrl.pathname)
00115| // And redirect to the new URL
00116| return NextResponse.redirect(loginUrl)
00117| ```
00118| 
00119| ## `rewrite()`
00120| 
00121| Produce a response that rewrites (proxies) the given [URL](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/URL) while preserving the original URL.
00122| 
00123| ```ts
00124| import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
00125| 
00126| // Incoming request: /about, browser shows /about
00127| // Rewritten request: /proxy, browser shows /about
00128| return NextResponse.rewrite(new URL('/proxy', request.url))
00129| ```
00130| 
00131| ## `next()`
00132| 
00133| The `next()` method is useful for Proxy, as it allows you to return early and continue routing.
00134| 
00135| ```ts
00136| import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
00137| 
00138| return NextResponse.next()
00139| ```
00140| 
00141| You can also forward `headers` upstream when producing the response, using `NextResponse.next({ request: { headers } })`:
00142| 
00143| ```ts
00144| import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
00145| 
00146| // Given an incoming request...
00147| const newHeaders = new Headers(request.headers)
00148| // Add a new header
00149| newHeaders.set('x-version', '123')
00150| // Forward the modified request headers upstream
00151| return NextResponse.next({
00152|   request: {
00153|     // New request headers
00154|     headers: newHeaders,
00155|   },
00156| })
00157| ```
00158| 
00159| This forwards `newHeaders` upstream to the target page, route, or server action, and does not expose them to the client. While this pattern is useful for passing data upstream, it should be used with caution because the headers containing this data may be forwarded to external services.
00160| 
00161| In contrast, `NextResponse.next({ headers })` is a shorthand for sending headers from proxy to the client. This is **NOT** good practice and should be avoided. Among other reasons because setting response headers like `Content-Type`, can override framework expectations (for example, the `Content-Type` used by Server Actions), leading to failed submissions or broken streaming responses.
00162| 
00163| ```ts
00164| import { type NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server'
00165| 
00166| async function proxy(request: NextRequest) {
00167|   const headers = await injectAuth(request.headers)
00168|   // DO NOT forward headers like this
00169|   return NextResponse.next({ headers })
00170| }
00171| ```
00172| 
00173| In general, avoid copying all incoming request headers because doing so can leak sensitive data to clients or upstream services.
00174| 
00175| Prefer a defensive approach by creating a subset of incoming request headers using an allow-list. For example, you might discard custom `x-*` headers and only forward known-safe headers:
00176| 
00177| ```ts
00178| import { type NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server'
00179| 
00180| function proxy(request: NextRequest) {
00181|   const incoming = new Headers(request.headers)
00182|   const forwarded = new Headers()
00183| 
00184|   for (const [name, value] of incoming) {
00185|     const headerName = name.toLowerCase()
00186|     // Keep only known-safe headers, discard custom x-* and other sensitive ones

The `notFound` function throws an error that renders a Next.js 404 page. It's useful for handling missing resources in your application. You can customize the UI using the [`not-found.js` file](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/not-found).

Invoking `notFound()` throws a `NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK;404` error and terminates rendering of the route segment where it was thrown. Next.js also injects a `<meta name="robots" content="noindex" />` tag so the page is not indexed. Because it works by throwing, call it in the render path: a component, or a function a component `await`s. A call left in an un-awaited promise throws where nothing catches it, and no not-found UI renders (in development the server logs `⨯ unhandledRejection: NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK;404`).
